resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance (COC), Home Re-Sale or Rental
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Waldwick Building Department (Construction Department)
resale_co.lead_time: Fee depends on how soon the inspection is needed (more than 14 days out is cheapest). The FAQ suggests applying 2 to 3 weeks before closing. Inspections by appointment, Monday to Friday 10 AM to 12 PM (FAQ). Certificate issued on site at the inspection.
resale_co.valid_for: Six (6) months or until another change in occupancy, whichever comes first
requirements: Handrails on steps of four risers or more
Sump pump connections removed from sewer piping
All open permits closed; newly installed furnace, water heater, roof, siding, finished basement, electrical or plumbing work must have had permits
Garages converted without permit or approval must be returned to usable garage (written proof required)
Smoke alarms on each floor and CO alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas; the department witnesses the owner's test of all smoke detectors
Portable fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (Building page and FAQ still list it)
Final water meter reading and final water bill before closing

fees.label: COC inspection, more than 14 days out
COC inspection within 14 days (11 to 14 days)
COC inspection within 10 days (4 to 10 days)
Reinspection after a failure or a no-show
fees.quote: A Re-inspection fee of $15.00 will apply to COC Failure and no show appointments.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Compliance Home Re-Sale or Rental Application (page 2 of the COC Inspections PDF on the Building page) and pay by check (no cash) at the Building Department, 63 Franklin Turnpike. Call (201) 652-5300 x240 for the final water bill.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official, Zoning Official (Technical Assistant: Nancy Koch, ext:232, nkoch@waldwicknj.gov)

evidence.quote: State law requires an inspection of the smoke alarm(s), carbon monoxide alarm(s) and portable fire extinguisher(s) before the sale, transfer or rental of residential property can occur
Certificates are issued on site at the time of inspection and are valid for six (6) months or until another change in occupancy occurs, whichever comes first.
Sump pump connections are to be removed from sewer piping.
COC inspections within 3 days, $200.00, 4-10 days: $150.00, 11-14 days $75.00
We recommend that the homeowner (or agent) visit the Building Department 2-3 weeks before the closing date to apply for a COC.

resale_co.notes: Waldwick runs one Certificate of Compliance through the Building Department that covers the state smoke/CO certificate plus local items (handrails, sump pumps, open permits, sidewalks, garage conversions). The Building FAQ still says the fee is $50, which is older than the $55.00 base fee on the current COC form. The Borough code section for this certificate was not checked.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each floor; 10-year sealed battery single station alarms (ANSI/UL 217) where battery alarms are used; AC alarms from original construction or rehabilitation may not be replaced with battery alarms
CO alarm within 10 feet of sleeping areas
Portable fire extinguisher (Building page and FAQ still list it; FAQ says within 10 feet of the kitchen)
Owner or representative performs the test of every smoke detector while the department watches

authorities.name: Borough of Waldwick Building Department (Certificate of Compliance); Waldwick Fire Prevention Bureau is the fire code agency
authorities.lead_time: More than 14 days out for the lowest fee. Certificate issued on site, valid six months.

fees.label: COC inspection, more than 14 days out
COC inspection within 14 days (11 to 14 days)
COC inspection within 10 days (4 to 10 days)
Reinspection after a failure or a no-show
fees.quote: A Re-inspection fee of $15.00 will apply to COC Failure and no show appointments.

authorities.how_to_apply: Smoke and CO alarms are checked in the Building Department's COC inspection; use the COC application and pay by check. Owner or representative must test all detectors while the inspector watches. Have the alarm specifications and installation instructions on hand.
authorities.contact_title: Building Department; Fire Official James O'Connell (201-652-5300 x249) leads the Fire Prevention Bureau

evidence.quote: State law requires and inspection of the smoke alarm(s) and carbon monoxide alarm(s) before the sale, transfer or rental of residential property can occur
This Department is required to witness the test of all smoke detectors within the home.
other than those structures which are owner occupied one-and two-family dwellings.

fire_cert.notes: The state directory lists the Waldwick Building Department as the smoke detector compliance office, and the COC form is the Building Department's. The Fire Prevention Bureau sheet gives joconnell@waldwicknj.org; the state directory gives joconnell@waldwicknj.gov. The Building page and FAQ still mention a portable fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed from the sale certificate in February 2025; confirm with the department.

other_items.label: Final water reading
other_items.detail: Final water meter reading is due before closing; call (201) 652-5300 x240 for the final water bill.

other_items.label: Sidewalks and sump pump
other_items.detail: Sidewalks must be in good condition and sump pump connections must be removed from sewer piping before the COC is issued.

open_questions: Does Waldwick still require the portable fire extinguisher after P.L.2025, c.19?
